- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative (0.3–0.6) and price is consolidating; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; if true outcome shows strong upward trend in last 5–7 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–3% higher than model’s final 10-day projection.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.2 per day), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead, not lagging behind.
